comments.author: @igguilloda4383
comments.text: these videos that try to explain the "why?" of why chile is the shape that it is completely ignore the history, even if this is a geography video.  colonial chile does not resemble modern chile.  chile was relatively compact during colonial times and early independence before expanding north due to war of the pacific and then expanding south when the mapuche surrendered to the chilean state.  and as far as spain not governing over mountain ranges, min 3:40 this is not entirely true.  the provinces in what is now argentina of mendoza, santa fe, and san luis were administered from chile between the middle 1500s and the 1760s & 1770s.

comments.author: @jdillon8360
comments.text: A clarification on the width of the country at Puerto Natales. The mainland territory of Chile might only be 10 miles wide there, but that's not the pacific ocean that Puerto Natales faces. Rather it's a small gulf. Chilean territory, made up of islands, ice sheets, fjords, etc, continues for another 130 miles west approximately, before reaching the Pacific.
